blocks.text:
Read these before anything that uses them.
Components are read against declared directions: x counts east and y counts north. Nothing in this bucket has a component until those directions are stated.
A magnitude is written without a sign and a component is written with one. Both describe the same vector, and swapping them is the error this bucket exists to prevent.

This bucket covers Reading a vector as a signed component pair against declared axes, re-declaring those axes, and subtracting one vector from another by construction.
Deliberately excluded: Rotated axes. PHY-VEC-AXIS-CONVENTION holds axes perpendicular and non-rotating under a re-declaration, so a rotated-axis treatment sits outside this bucket.
Deliberately excluded: The direction of a zero resultant. PHY-VEC-SUBTRACTION states that a zero resultant has none, so none is assigned here.

blocks.meaning: Subtracting a vector means adding its reverse; component-wise this is (P-Q)_x = P_x - Q_x and (P-Q)_y = P_y - Q_y.
symbols: P: First vector in a named common frame
Q: Second vector in the same frame
-Q: Q reversed: same magnitude, opposite direction
conditions: P and Q are expressed along the same declared axes.
Reversal preserves magnitude and negates every component.
Free vectors may be translated without rotation for the graphical construction.

correspondence.in_words: the vector being subtracted from, drawn from the frame's origin
the vector being taken away, before it is turned around
the same arrow pointing the other way, the same length as before

scene.frame: One common east/north frame, at one length scale for every vector drawn.
scene.caption: P - Q is built by reversing Q and placing it at the head of P. The resultant (6, -8) m/s is longer than either vector, which a component-subtraction shortcut gives without ever showing why.

blocks.text:
Where the hard work is.
Vector information versus magnitude-only information. (MEDIUM) The words are simple, but learners often treat equal length or equal speed as if it fully identifies a directed quantity.
Choosing axes and keeping components signed. (MEDIUM) Axis choice is conventional, but once the positive directions are declared the component signs are fixed and cannot be chosen for convenience.
Subtraction as addition of the reversed vector. (MEDIUM) The reverse-then-add construction is a genuine model shift from ordinary addition, even though the component arithmetic looks similar.
